summary: On node1, /srv/data is now backed by a loopback-mounted Btrfs filesystem (no LVM/native-snapshot fs was available on the ext4 root), managed by a systemd oneshot unit (srv-data-btrfs.service) that reattaches the loop device and mounts the top-level subvolume plus the /data subvolume at boot. Application data was populated, a read-only Btrfs snapshot was taken as a baseline, the live directory was then modified (file corrupted, file deleted, extraneous file added), and the directory was restored via rsync --delete from the snapshot back to an exact byte-for-byte match of the baseline (verified by sha256). The node was then restarted using systemctl reboot; boot_id changed confirming a real restart, the mount service came back active/enabled automatically, the btrfs subvolumes (data + snapshot) survived, and /srv/data content was re-verified as byte-identical to the pre-restart baseline and to the snapshot subvolume.
actions_performed: Inspected node1 filesystem/storage (ext4 root, no LVM, btrfs-progs available) to choose a snapshot-capable backing store
Created a 2GB loopback-backed Btrfs image, top-level mount at /mnt/srv-data-btrfs, and a 'data' subvolume mounted at /srv/data via the same loop device
Authored /usr/local/sbin/srv-data-btrfs-{mount,umount}.sh and a systemd oneshot unit srv-data-btrfs.service (enabled, WantedBy=local-fs.target) for reboot-safe remounting
Validated cold-start mount via manual umount + systemctl start
Populated /srv/data with application data (config, important.txt, logs) and recorded sha256 baseline
Took a read-only btrfs snapshot of /srv/data as the recovery point
Modified live data (corrupted a file, deleted a file, added an unexpected file) to simulate data loss/corruption
Restored /srv/data from the snapshot via rsync -a --delete and verified byte-identical sha256 match plus zero diff against the snapshot subvolume
Captured pre-restart boot_id and health baseline (mount active, data checksums, subvolume list)
Restarted node1 via systemctl reboot (non-blocking) and polled until exec was available again
Verified changed boot_id proving an actual restart occurred
Verified post-restart recovery: mount service active/enabled, both mounts present, btrfs subvolumes intact, and /srv/data content byte-identical to the pre-restart/snapshot baseline

evidence.requirement: Baseline: /srv/data snapshot-capable storage set up and healthy before modification
evidence.summary: Confirmed no LVM/native snapshot fs on root; built loop-mounted btrfs volume, validated cold-start mount via systemd unit, populated data and recorded sha256 baseline, then took a read-only btrfs snapshot capturing that baseline

evidence.requirement: Directory modified after snapshot, then restored to exact snapshot content
evidence.summary: Live /srv/data was corrupted/deleted/augmented, diff showed divergence from the snapshot, rsync --delete restored from the snapshot, and sha256 + diff -rq confirmed the restored directory is byte-identical to both the original baseline and the snapshot subvolume

evidence.requirement: Node restart: healthy pre-restart baseline captured
evidence.summary: Captured pre-restart boot_id (901ef286...), active mount service, active btrfs mounts, data checksums, and subvolume list as the healthy baseline

evidence.requirement: Node restart: restart acknowledged and boot identity changed
evidence.summary: Issued non-blocking systemctl reboot (ack returned before disconnect), then polled node1 until exec responded again; boot_id changed to b3b233b6... and uptime showed 0 minutes, proving an actual restart

evidence.requirement: Node restart: post-restart recovery of required services/data/mount
evidence.summary: Post-restart: srv-data-btrfs.service active+enabled, both btrfs mounts present, subvolumes (data + snapshot) intact, and /srv/data sha256 checksums matched the pre-restart/snapshot baseline exactly (diff clean)
